title: Second Conditional: if + Past Simple, would
grammarTitle: Second Conditional — Imaginary and Hypothetical Situations
grammarNote: Second Conditional (второе условное предложение) используется для воображаемых, маловероятных или нереальных ситуаций в настоящем или будущем. Оно выражает: ① советы ("If I were you..."), ② мечты и желания, ③ маловероятные сценарии. Структура: IF + Past Simple, WOULD + base verb.

grammarTable.subject: If clause (condition)
grammarTable.example: "If I had more money..." / "If she lived in Almaty..." / "If we knew..."

grammarTable.subject: Negative condition
grammarTable.example: "If I didn't have to work, I'd study more." / "If she weren't so busy..."

grammarTable.subject: Negative result
grammarTable.example: "If I were rich, I wouldn't stay in this flat."

grammarTable.subject: Question form
grammarTable.example: "What would you do if you had the money?" / "Would you go if she invited you?"

grammarTable.subject: "were" for all subjects
grammarTable.example: "If I were you..." / "If she were here..." / "If it were possible..."

rows.example: "If I lived in London, I'd go to the theatre every week." (I don't live there)

rows.form: ② Advice: If I were you...
rows.example: "If I were you, I'd take the research position." (giving advice)
"If I won the lottery, I'd travel the world." (very unlikely)
"If she called me right now, I'd be surprised." (unlikely to happen)
"If I had time, I'd definitely go." (definite)
"If I had time, I could visit her." (it would be possible)
"If I had time, I might go." (perhaps, not certain)
"If you had the chance, you should try it." (advice/recommendation)
"If I WERE you, I'd take it." (ALL subjects → were in formal English)
"If I WAS rich, I'd buy a house." (acceptable in everyday speech)
The expression "If I were you" is ALWAYS "were" — never "If I was you" in formal English.
"If it were/was possible, I'd move to Edinburgh." (both acceptable)
✅ "If I HAD money..." — NEVER use "would" in the IF clause!

rows.form: ✗ "If I have more time, I'd go."
rows.example: ✅ "If I HAD more time, I'd go." — Past Simple (had), not Present Simple.

rows.form: ✗ "I would go if I will have time."
rows.example: ✅ "I would go if I HAD time." — Past Simple in if-clause always.

rows.form: ✗ "If I were you, I will take it."
rows.example: ✅ "If I were you, I'd (would) take it." — always "would" in result.

grammarTip:
Second Conditional — структура:
IF + PAST SIMPLE → WOULD + BASE VERB

"If I HAD the money, I WOULD travel."
"If she LIVED here, she WOULD be happier."

⚠️ Главные ошибки:
① НИКОГДА не пиши "would" в if-части:
✗ "If I would have money..." → ✅ "If I HAD money..."
② В if-части PAST SIMPLE, не Present Simple:
✗ "If I have time, I'd go." → ✅ "If I HAD time, I'd go."

💡 Специальный случай: "If I were you" — ВСЕГДА were
→ "If I were you, I'd take the research position."

💡 Would может заменяться на could (возможность), might (неопределённость):
"If I had time, I COULD visit you." / "I MIGHT go."

exercises.text: If Kamila ___ (have) the money, she ___ (study) in Scotland.
exercises.hint: If + PAST SIMPLE (had) + WOULD + base verb. "If she HAD the money, she WOULD STUDY in Scotland." ✅

exercises.text: "If I ___ (be) you, I ___ (take) the research position." (advice)
exercises.hint: "If I WERE you, I WOULD TAKE the research position." — classic 2nd conditional advice. ✅

exercises.text: "If I would have more time, I'd travel more." — What is wrong?
opts: "would" in the if-clause — should be Past Simple "had"
exercises.correct: "would" in the if-clause — should be Past Simple "had"
exercises.hint: ✅ "If I HAD more time, I'd travel more." — NEVER "would" in the if-clause! ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal for an uncertain result.
exercises.text: "If I had the money, I ___ go to Edinburgh — but I'm not sure yet."
exercises.hint: "might" = uncertain result (perhaps). "If I had the money, I MIGHT go." ✅ ("would" = certain; "might" = uncertain)

exercises.text: "What ___ you ___ (do) if you had a million tenge?" (second conditional)
exercises.hint: "What WOULD you DO if you had a million tenge?" ✅ (would + subject + base verb)

exercises.text: "If she ___ (live) in Uralsk, she ___ (know) the city well."
exercises.hint: If + PAST SIMPLE (lived) + WOULD + base verb. "If she LIVED in Uralsk, she WOULD KNOW the city well." ✅

exercises.text: "If I have the money, I'd travel." is a correct Second Conditional.
exercises.hint: ✅ "If I HAD the money, I'd travel." — use Past Simple "had", not Present Simple "have".

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct negative Second Conditional.
exercises.text: "If I ___ (not / have) to work, I ___ (study) more."
exercises.hint: "If I DIDN'T HAVE to work, I WOULD STUDY more." — Negative if-clause: didn't + base verb. ✅

exercises.text: "If she had a car, she ___ (drive) to Aktobe in four hours."
exercises.hint: "If she had a car, she COULD DRIVE to Aktobe." = it would be possible. ✅

exercises.instruction: Which sentence is correct Second Conditional?
opts: "If I would have more money, I'd invest it."
"If I had more money, I would invest it."
"If I have more money, I would invest it."
"If I had more money, I will invest it."
exercises.correct: "If I had more money, I would invest it."
exercises.hint: "If I HAD more money, I WOULD INVEST it." — Past Simple + would + base verb. ✅

opts: "If I was you, I will take it."
"If I were you, I would take it."
"If I be you, I would take it."
"If I were you, I will take it."
exercises.correct: "If I were you, I would take it."
exercises.hint: "If I WERE you, I WOULD TAKE it." — always "were" + would. ✅

exercises.text: "If Rustam ___ (win) the lottery, he ___ (travel) all over Central Asia."
exercises.hint: "If Rustam WON the lottery, he WOULD TRAVEL all over Central Asia." ✅

questions.text: "If she had the money, she ___ study in Scotland." Complete.
questions.hint: 2nd Conditional: if + Past Simple → WOULD + base verb. "...she WOULD study." ✅

questions.text: "If I ___ you, I'd take the offer." (advice)
questions.hint: "If I WERE you" — special form for advice. "Were" for all subjects in formal 2nd Conditional. ✅

questions.text: "If I would have more time, I'd go." is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "If I HAD more time, I'd go." — NEVER "would" in the if-clause!

questions.text: "If Amir ___ (not / work), he'd study more." Choose correctly.
questions.hint: Negative if-clause: DIDN'T + base verb. "If Amir DIDN'T WORK, he'd study more." ✅

questions.text: "What would you do if you ___ (have) a million tenge?"
questions.hint: 2nd Conditional: if + PAST SIMPLE. "...if you HAD a million tenge?" ✅

questions.text: "If she had time, she ___ visit us." (it would be possible)
questions.hint: "could" = it would be possible. "If she had time, she COULD visit us." ✅

questions.text: "If she had time, she ___ visit us." (maybe, uncertain)
questions.hint: "might" = uncertain/possible. "If she had time, she MIGHT visit us." ✅

questions.text: "If he ___ (live) closer, he ___ (not / take) the bus every day."
questions.hint: "If he LIVED closer, he WOULDN'T TAKE the bus." — Past Simple + wouldn't + base. ✅

opts: Imaginary/hypothetical situations in the present or future
questions.correct: Imaginary/hypothetical situations in the present or future
questions.hint: 2nd Conditional = imaginary, unlikely, or hypothetical. Not real current plans.

questions.text: "If I were rich, I wouldn't stay here." — "were" is used because:
questions.hint: "were" in 2nd Conditional = hypothetical subjunctive. "If I WERE rich" = imaginary situation. ✅

questions.text: Which sentence is the correct Second Conditional?
opts: "If I would have money, I'd travel."
"If I had money, I will travel."
questions.hint: "If I HAD money, I'D TRAVEL." — Past Simple + would. ✅

questions.text: "If Zhibek ___ (be) a professional athlete, she ___ (need) more training."
questions.hint: "If Zhibek WERE a professional athlete, she WOULD NEED more training." ✅

questions.text: "Would you travel if you had more money?" — This is:
questions.hint: "if you HAD more money" = Past Simple → Second Conditional. "WOULD you travel?" ✅

questions.text: "I'd" in "I'd take it" is short for:
questions.hint: "I'd" = "I would" (contracted form). Very common in spoken and informal English. ✅

questions.text: "If he ___ (not / live) far away, we ___ (see) him more often."
questions.hint: "If he DIDN'T LIVE far away, we WOULD SEE him more often." ✅

questions.text: What is NEVER in the if-clause of a Second Conditional?
questions.hint: NEVER "would" in the if-clause! ✅ "If I would have..." = ✗. Always Past Simple: "If I had..." ✅
